text:
Edmonton has not won in five games, and it is about to play the team that extended the streak, again, 24 hours later. Seattle won 4-2 in Edmonton last night even though the replays liked the Oilers: they won 66% of the simulations of that game's shots. That is the frustrating part of this slump for Mike Babcock's team. Over the five games they have been outscored 24-14, but two of them were nights they outchanced the other side.

Here is the tension in the standings. The Oilers still sit on 38 points and our numbers give them 95% to make the playoffs, largely because they have scored 24.8 more goals than their chances usually produce. Their five-on-five share of expected goals, the quality of chances, is only 47%. A team living on finishing can survive a cold week; what it cannot do is keep giving away territory. Babcock has been leaning on Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl together, and he explained why in a clip Oilersnation posted: "When I don't have Nuge, when I don't have enough centres, I'm in a tough spot." Ryan Nugent-Hopkins is back now, and with Zach Hyman out, he has moved beside Colton Dach and Kasperi Kapanen.

Seattle's story is younger. Berkly Catton, 20, has been the most written-about Kraken player of the last two weeks, with a hat trick against Vancouver along the way, and Kaapo Kakko has eight points in his last 10. The Kraken are 3-2-0 in their last five with 54% of the expected goals, a real improvement on a season share of 45%. Jared McCann is out until January.

Jordan Eberle, drafted by Edmonton in 2008, is one point from 800 for his career, and the old team is in the building. Joey Daccord and Devon Levi are both slightly below expected this season, so neither crease has bailed anyone out. Draisaitl is our likeliest scorer at 51%.
headline: The Oilers try again against the Kraken
